'''Jon Azkargorta Aretxabala''' (born in [[Algorta]], [[Getxo]], on 3 May 1963) is a Spanish former rugby union player. He played as centre or as fullback. He was nicknamed "Azkar".

==Career==
Azkargorta always played for [[Getxo Artea RT]] from his hometown. He formed part the only [[División de Honor de Rugby|División de Honor]] title on the club's cabinet, in the 1992–93 season, and several [[Copa del Rey de Rugby|Copa del Rey]] titles. In 1986 he was one of the members of the first [[Spain national rugby sevens team|Spain sevens]] team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jon Azkargorta Aretxabala|url=http://www.espnscrum.com/scrum/rugby/player/9543.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=ESPN scrum|archive-date=2023-03-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319114618/http://en.espn.co.uk/scrum/rugby/player/9543.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He is the second player with most caps (76) in the story of the Spain national team, only after [[Francisco Puertas Soto|Francisco Puertas]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Comité Olímpico Español|url=https://www.coe.es/COE/bd_perso.nsf/2012FDeportistaN3?OpenForm&query=10642*&DEPORTISTA=7583*|access-date=2020-11-21|website=www.coe.es}}</ref> He was first capped against [[Argentina national rugby union team|Argentina]] in [[Madrid]], on 23 November 1982 and his last cap was against [[Wales national rugby union team]] on 21 May 1994, also played at [[Estadio Nacional Complutense]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jon Azkargorta Aretxabala|url=http://www.espnscrum.com/scrum/rugby/player/9543.html|access-date=2020-11-21|website=ESPN scrum|archive-date=2023-03-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319114618/http://en.espn.co.uk/scrum/rugby/player/9543.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Along with [[Asier Altuna Izaguirre|Asier Altuna]], [[Iñaki Laskurain]], [[Julio Álvarez (rugby union)|Julio Álvarez]], [[Francisco Puertas|Fran Puertas]], [[Javier Díaz Paternain]], [[Alberto Malo]], [[José Prieto Acevedo|José Prieto]] and [[José Ignacio Zapatero]], Azkargorta was also part of the Spain team which won the bronze medal at the [[Rugby union at the 1993 Mediterranean Games|1993 Mediterranean Games]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=. |title=Así / Jon Azkargorta: Así ganamos la medalla de los Mediterráneos de 1993 |url=https://www.apalos.es/2020/11/asi-jon-azkargorta-asi-ganamos-la_26.html |access-date=2026-11-01 |website=A PALOS}}</ref> coached by Gérard Murillo.

==Personal life==
Azkargorta is a physical teacher at the [[University of the Basque Country]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jon Azkargorta Aretxabala :: Inguma - Base de datos de la comunidad científica vasca|url=https://www.inguma.eus/egilea/ikusi/jon-azkargorta-aretxabala?page=1&hizkuntza=es|access-date=2020-11-21|website=www.inguma.eus|archive-date=2017-02-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215125911/https://www.inguma.eus/egilea/ikusi/jon-azkargorta-aretxabala?page=1&hizkuntza=es|url-status=live}}</ref>
